report.summary: Chunk 3 of inventory.py: implements build() to derive the full document, stale_features() for packaging ghosts and orphan bytecode, and i/o helpers load/write/refresh.

handoff.purpose: Define stale_features, build, load, write_inventory, and refresh functions.

symbols.name: stale_features
symbols.note: Defined earlier in the file; referenced in build()

symbols.name: build
symbols.note: Derives the whole document, writes nothing.

symbols.name: load
symbols.note: Loads JSON from file, returns dict or error dict.

symbols.name: write_inventory
symbols.note: Writes JSON to file, returns the string.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Regenerates inventory in place, carrying annotations forward.

claims.text: Derive the whole document. Writes nothing.
claims.why: build() returns a dict; no file writes in this function.

claims.text: ``reports`` is the ``(reach, switches)`` pair from :func:`daedalus.mapping.render.analyse_once`. When it is not supplied this calls that function -- which is the configuration the PRODUCT uses, index and all. Calling ``reach.analyse(root)`` with no index here would be a second engine configuration that ships to nobody, and the last time a guard did that a CRITICAL survived underneath it.
claims.why: The code calls render_mod.analyse_once(root, index) if reports is falsy, using the same index.

claims.text: Reported, NOT filed as a stale feature. Its remedy is 'add it to the list', the exact opposite verb from the stale remedy ('remove it'), and handing a fixer the wrong verb is how a finding becomes damage.
claims.why: gaps (on_disk_but_unlisted) are stored separately from stale_features; they are not added to the stale list.

claims.text: The prose summaries the previous schema carried. Derived from the SAME pass as the structured features, so the discrepancy the picker reports when the two disagree cannot occur by construction.
claims.where: build docstring comment inside doc dict
claims.why: The 'islands', 'shims', 'unknown', 'unreached', 'stale' keys are derived from the same reach_report and stale_features used for structured features.

claims.text: Regenerate in place, carrying the human half forward. The old document is read for its annotations BEFORE it is overwritten, and a first run over a schema-1 file harvests them out of the hand-written entries. Refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: refresh() calls load(target) first, then later (in next chunk) will write; annotations are harvested from old doc.

observations.what: build() uses render_mod.analyse_once but render_mod is imported late inside the function
load() returns None when file does not exist, but returns error dict on parse failure; refresh() checks for __error__
